To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the VGGs of benchmarks of Etnas monitoring system were predicted using the refined procedure, (2) the VGG predictions are improved, (3) the accuracy of the predictions is improved.

the accuracy of predicted vertical gradient of gravity values at a gravity network is improved by refining benchmark positions using precise geodetary methods, modeling and accounting for the gravitational effects of buildings and roadside wall adjacent to the benchmarks, and producing a new high-resolution DEM based on drone-flowned photogrammetry in the proximity of some benchmarks.

the accuracy of predicted VGG values can be improved considerably by (a) refining the benchmark positions using precise geodetics, (b) modeling the gravitational effect of buildings adjacent to benchmarks and (c) using high-resolution DEMs for the benchmarks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the refinement of the VGG prediction, which is a prerequisite to the use of the VGG as a gravity monitoring parameter for volcano deformation monitoring.
improving the prediction of VGG values at gravity monitoring networks, which is a prerequisite for the detection of small changes in gravity.
the refinement of the VGG prediction, which is an important component in the gravity network monitoring system at Etna Volcano.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VGG prediction is now accurate enough to be useful for the Etna volcano monitoring system.
the accuracy of the VGG predictions can be improved by a factor of three.
the VGG prediction accuracy at Etna’s network was improved by a factor of three, which was achieved through a combination of the three described refinements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a high-precision DEM is required for the VGG prediction in the innermost area at the Etna network, while in the outermost area, where the DEM is of lower resolution, the VGG values can be predicted using the DEM of the national mapping agency.

the accuracy of the VGG prediction can be improved by refining the DEM in the proximity of the benchmarks, by modeling the gravitational effect of the benchmark-neighborhood buildings and walls and by improving the accuracy of the benchmark positioning.
the VGG prediction can be improved by a combination of precise benchmark positioning, accounting for the gravitational effects of the adjacent buildings and walls, and high-resolution DEMs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful and detailed assessment of the VGG prediction is necessary to ensure the quality of the prediction at gravity networks.
the VGG prediction can be improved at the Etna volcano monitoring network and that the same improvements can be applied to other networks.
a high-resolution DEM is required for accurate prediction of the VGG at benchmarks located in urban areas.
